questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Fundamental Principles of Surveying & Linear Measurements
questions.text: State the fundamental principles of surveying: (a) Working from whole to part, and (b) Fixing position of a new point with respect to at least two reference points. Explain types of errors in surveying (Systematic / Cumulative errors vs. Accidental / Compensating errors) and differentiate between Precision and Accuracy.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Fundamental Principles of Surveying & Linear Measurements
questions.text: Explain tape corrections applied in precise linear measurements: (a) Temperature correction $C_t = \alpha(T_m - T_0)L$, (b) Pull correction $C_p = \frac{(P_m - P_0)L}{A E}$, (c) Sag correction $C_s = \frac{W^2 L}{24 P_m^2}$, and (d) Slope correction $C_h = \frac{h^2}{2L}$. A steel tape $30\,\text{m}$ long standard at $20^\circ\text{C}$ and $100\,\text{N}$ tension was used to measure a distance of $300\,\text{m}$ at $32^\circ\text{C}$ and $150\,\text{N}$ tension with 3 catenary bays. Calculate true distance.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Compass Surveying, Traversing & Local Attraction Adjustments
questions.text: Compare Prismatic Compass vs. Surveyor's Compass. Explain Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) and Reduced / Quadrantal Bearing (RB). What is Local Attraction in compass surveying? How is it detected from fore bearing and back bearing differences ($|FB - BB| = 180^\circ$) and eliminated by included angle method?

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Compass Surveying, Traversing & Local Attraction Adjustments
questions.text:
The following bearings were observed for a closed compass traverse $ABCDE$:
$AB: 74^\circ 20', BC: 107^\circ 20', CD: 224^\circ 50', DE: 306^\circ 40', EA: 33^\circ 50'$.
Detect the stations affected by local attraction, calculate the interior angles, and compute corrected fore and back bearings of all lines.

Explain Height of Instrument (Collimation) Method and Rise-and-Fall Method for booking and reducing leveling staff readings. State the mathematical checks for both methods: $\sum BS - \sum FS = \sum \text{Rise} - \sum \text{Fall} = \text{Last RL} - \text{First RL}$. Reduce the given leveling field book page and apply arithmetic checks.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Fundamental Principles of Surveying & Linear Measurements
questions.text: Explain Reciprocal Leveling. Show how reciprocal leveling eliminates errors due to: (a) Earth's curvature ($C_c = 0.0785 d^2$), (b) Atmospheric refraction ($C_r = 0.0112 d^2$), and (c) Imperfect adjustment of collimation line in the level.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Contouring, Contour Interpolation & Topographical Mapping
questions.text: Define Contour, Contour Line, Contour Interval, and Horizontal Equivalent. State 6 characteristics of contour lines with neat sketches (Ridge line, Valley line, Uniform slope, Overhanging cliff, Vertical cliff, Saddle). Explain methods of contour interpolation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Compass Surveying, Traversing & Local Attraction Adjustments
questions.text: Explain the temporary adjustments of a Transit Theodolite (Setting up, Leveling, Elimination of Parallax). Explain the method of Repetition and method of Reiteration for measuring horizontal angles with high precision.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Compass Surveying, Traversing & Local Attraction Adjustments
questions.text: Define Latitude ($L = l \cos\theta$) and Departure ($D = l \sin\theta$). Explain Bowditch's (Compass) Rule ($\delta L = \frac{\sum L}{\sum l} l_i$) and Transit Rule for balancing a closed theodolite traverse. Calculate the closing error $e = \sqrt{(\sum L)^2 + (\sum D)^2}$ and relative error of closure $\frac{1}{\sum l / e}$ for the given traverse data.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Fundamental Principles of Surveying & Linear Measurements
questions.text: Explain obstacles in chaining: (a) Chaining free, vision obstructed, (b) Chaining obstructed, vision free (e.g. river), and (c) Both chaining and vision obstructed (e.g. building). Show how distance across a wide river is measured using geometric constructions.
